title: Release handoff field notebook and nightshift cues (Nov 2026) - draft
content:
Purpose: quick-reference field notebook to run the night shift handoff for the Nov 2026 release. This doc is intentionally concise — the goal is to give on-call engineers and release shepherds a single-sheet view for preflight, cutover steps, fast diagnostics, and post-release sampling. Treat as a living runbook; update the 'open questions' section with any unresolved blockers.

Scope: Targeting hosted API + Dedicated pool change for model routing (optics v2). Private deploys are out-of-scope for this window.

Owners and primary contacts:
- Release lead: Arjun Patel (pager: arjun.r)
- Release conductor, on-site: Maya Chen (pager: maya.c)
- Nightshift lead (00:00–08:00 PT): Liam O'Connell
- SRE runbook backup: Sofia Ramirez
- PM for feature: Elena Novak

Quick calendar (compact):
- Fri 2026-11-05 18:00 PT — Preflight window opens: smoke runs, canary traffic 1%
- Sat 2026-11-06 00:00 PT — Night shift handoff: full cutover to routing-optics-v2, 4-hr observation
- Sat 2026-11-06 04:00 PT — If stable, increase to 25% traffic
- Sat 2026-11-06 08:00 PT — Day team resume checks, post-cutover retrospective checkpoint
- Sat 2026-11-13 12:00 PT — 1-week postmortem & quality sampling

Preflight checklist (complete before handoff):
- [ ] Canary artifact built and checksum verified (SHA256)
- [ ] Infra templates validated: autoscale policies + burst capacity test
- [ ] Telemetry flags added to rollout: rollout_id, deploy_tag
- [ ] Load test run with representative token distributions (see linked artifact)
- [ ] Canary runbook posted to #release-orbit channel
- [ ] Backout artifacts staged (previous model bundle ID + routing config)

Cutover steps (nightshift quick script):
1. Announce start: post to #release-orbit with timeline and deploy_tag
2. Apply routing config to 2 nodes in region-us-west2 (canary nodes)
3. Wait 90s; validate: p99 latency <= SLO (120ms hosted), error rate < 0.2%
4. If validation passes, scale routing to 12 nodes (25% traffic). If fails, execute rollback matrix below.
5. During scale, run flood-sampling job for 10 minutes to capture outputs for quality evals
6. Record any 'interesting' request ids in the release log (prefix RLOG/nov-06-night)

Nightshift cues (what to watch for):
- Telemetry: sudden jump in 'queue_time' or 'retry_count'
- SLOs: sustained p99 > 200ms for >5 minutes
- Errors: surge in 5xx, or client error patterns (400s) with new routing
- Optional: model output drift flag from quality monitor (if triggered, open a QL ticket)
- External signals: PagerDuty escalation from infra (treat as priority)

Rollback matrix (fast options):
- Minor spike in latency (p99 120–200ms, no error rise): Throttle rollout (move back to 10% traffic), set longer observation window + consult runtime logs
- Errors >0.5% or p50 increase + user-facing regression: Immediate rollback to previous routing config (apply rollback script: rollback-routing.sh <prev_tag>) and notify stakeholders
- Persistent KV cache desync across nodes: Rollback and run 'kv-resync' maintenance job; increase cache TTL as temporary mitigant

Communication script (short posts for Slack):
- Start: "Release 'optics-v2' start @ 2026-11-06 00:00 PT — canary -> partial routing. Watch p99/5xx on /v1/generate. Oncall: Liam O'C."
- Rollforward: "Progressing: lenses to 25% traffic at 04:00 PT — monitoring window open."
- Rollback: "Rollback executed — reverted to routing tag optics-v1-2026-10-28. Investigating."
- Done: "Cutover complete. Post-cutover checks green. Postmortem scheduled for 2026-11-13 12:00 PT."

Post-release sampling & notes (first 8 hours):
- Run regression sampling job 'quality-sample-nov06' capturing: 500 random host requests, 200 business-critical prompt families, and 50 adversarial prompts (from eval set)
- Collect cost delta report for dedicated pool (expected +3–5%)
- Note any qualitative user-facing regressions in this doc under 'issues-observed'

Draft release notes (blurb for external release notes / PR to docs):
- "Optics v2: improved routing heuristics for multi-model deployments. Expected benefits: 10–20% p99 latency reduction for busty traffic and improved tail predictability. No user-visible API changes."
- Known limits: first-hour small chance of transient p99 spikes during KV warm-up. Rolling back is fast; no schema changes.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Who will own final canary sign-off if day team is unavailable? (TODO: confirm with Elena)
- Confirm Dedicated pool capacity budget for burst (TODO: finance approval by 11/04)
- Add a short checklist for Private deploys parity (separate doc)

Issues observed (placeholder; populate during night):
- <empty> — use RLOG/nov-06-night prefixed notes

After-action items (assignments):
- Arjun: finalize rollback script and ensure perms tested (due 2026-11-04)
- Maya: update the canary dashboard with 'deploy_tag' filter (due 2026-11-05)
- Liam: prepare 00:00–08:00 shard monitoring rotation and handoff notes (due 2026-11-05)
- SRE: snapshot cluster state post-cutover and upload to shared bucket

References & quick links:
- Jira: RINF-2145 (deploy optics routing)
- PR: runtime#1892 (routing heuristics + telemetry flags)
- Confluence: Release Orbit - Nov 2026
- Slack thread: #release-orbit (pin: 'nov-optics-preflight')

Revision history:
- 2026-11-03 Arjun Patel — initial draft
- 2026-11-05 Maya Chen — added nightshift cues and rollback matrix
- 2026-11-07 Liam O'Connell — clarified communication scripts and sampling plan

Notes to self: keep the field notebook minimal — engineers on nights prefer bullet lists and explicit guardrails. If a new 'drift' signal appears, escalate to PM and Research immediately.
